newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower, recent gains consolidated.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower, recent gains consolidated.

text.p: Swiss shares ended easier on Monday in thin volume as recent gains were consolidated, dealers said.
"Today's correction was no surprise given the high level of the bourse," one trader said, pointing out that the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) posted a record high on Friday.
The outcome of Tuesday's host of U.S. data and the further development of Wall Street would give the market new direction, one trader said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 22.6 points, or 0.42 points, to 5,362.0.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended lower by 13.76 points or 0.4 percent at 3,406.80.
Bourse volume was 1.79 billion Swiss francs. Trade was dominated by professionals, dealers said.
Sulzer shares were sought, profiting from the company's long-awaited information in the IPO of its medical unit.
Sulzer said bookbuilding for Sulzer Medica shares will start on June 30 and trading is expected to commence in the week of July 14.
Sulzer shareholders will have the right to buy one Medica share for every 10 Sulzer shares. Sulzer stocks added 10 francs to 1,340 after reaching an all-time high at 1,384.
Swiss Re were lifted by the completion of a large sell order, adding six francs at 1,966.
Novartis gave up two francs to 2,088. Roche was off 85 francs to 12,955.
Among financials, CS Holding was still pressured by sells of disgrountled investors who had pinned their hopes on recent merger and spin-off speculation. UBS was down 16 francs at 1,679.
Surveillance rebounded from recent losses, adding 85 francs to 3,100.
